To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the architecture of the network is not important, as long as it is simple; 2) the training objective is not important, either; 3) the only important aspect is the loss that is applied to the generated output.

the use of a simple architecture, with skip connections, and the use of a perceptual loss function, based on features extracted from an intermediate layer in a deep neural network, can be used to solve many image-to-image translation tasks.
the use of a single generator with a multi-layer discriminator is sufficient to address a variety of unpaired translation tasks, and that the use of an additional encoder is unnecessary.
